title: Draft: hyperdht: add DHT-RPC and HyperDHT dissector
description:
## Summary

- Add heuristic UDP dissection for DHT-RPC and HyperDHT.
- Decode internal RPC and application commands, structured values, errors, and plugin payloads.
- Track request/response frames, response time, and PING_NAT cross-port flows.
- Add a deterministic 38-frame capture and focused pytest coverage.

## Validation

- Fork merge-request pipeline: https://gitlab.com/quetzalforge/wireshark/-/pipelines/2739202214
  - 6/6 jobs passed.
  - Clang + Code Checks, Clang ASAN, Ubuntu GCC, no-options build, commit checks, and AI trailer check passed.
  - GitLab reported 2,892 test cases.
- Local Windows UCRT64 build completed with `-Werror`.
- `test/suite_dissectors/group_hyperdht.py`: 3 passed.
- The HyperDHT upstream JavaScript test suite passed: 91/91.

## Attribution

The initial dissector work was authored by James Thomas and is credited with a `Co-authored-by` trailer in the commit.

Assisted-by: Codex

@@ -0,0 +1,130 @@
+# Wireshark tests for the DHT-RPC and HyperDHT dissector
+# Copyright 2026, Gustavo Zepeda
+#
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+"""DHT-RPC and HyperDHT dissector tests."""
+
+import subprocess
+
+
+def _frames(cmd_tshark, capture, display_filter, test_env):
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        (
+            cmd_tshark,
+            "-r",
+            capture,
+            "-Y",
+            display_filter,
+            "-T",
+            "fields",
+            "-e",
+            "frame.number",
+        ),
+        capture_output=True,
+        check=True,
+        encoding="utf-8",
+        env=test_env,
+    )
+    return result.stdout.splitlines()
+
+
+def _links(cmd_tshark, capture, field, test_env):
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        (
+            cmd_tshark,
+            "-2",
+            "-r",
+            capture,
+            "-Y",
+            field,
+            "-T",
+            "fields",
+            "-E",
+            "separator=|",
+            "-e",
+            "frame.number",
+            "-e",
+            field,
+        ),
+        capture_output=True,
+        check=True,
+        encoding="utf-8",
+        env=test_env,
+    )
+    return [tuple(int(value) for value in line.split("|")) for line in result.stdout.splitlines()]
+
+
+class TestHyperDHT:
+    def test_all_commands_and_heuristic(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        capture = capture_file("hyperdht.pcapng")
+
+        assert _frames(cmd_tshark, capture, "hyperdht", test_env) == [str(i) for i in range(1, 37)]
+        assert _frames(cmd_tshark, capture, "frame.number >= 37 && hyperdht", test_env) == []
+
+        expected_counts = {
+            0: 2,
+            1: 2,
+            2: 2,
+            3: 2,
+            4: 2,
+            5: 2,
+            6: 2,
+            7: 2,
+            8: 2,
+            9: 2,
+            10: 4,
+            256: 2,
+            257: 2,
+            258: 2,
+            259: 2,
+            260: 2,
+        }
+        for command, count in expected_counts.items():
+            frames = _frames(cmd_tshark, capture, f"hyperdht.command == {command}", test_env)
+            assert len(frames) == count, f"unexpected frame count for command {command}"
+
+    def test_request_response_links(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        capture = capture_file("hyperdht.pcapng")
+        expected_requests = [(frame, frame + 1) for frame in range(1, 36, 2)]
+        expected_responses = [(frame, frame - 1) for frame in range(2, 37, 2)]
+
+        assert _links(cmd_tshark, capture, "hyperdht.response_in", test_env) == expected_requests
+        assert _links(cmd_tshark, capture, "hyperdht.request_in", test_env) == expected_responses
+        assert _frames(
+            cmd_tshark,
+            capture,
+            "frame.number == 6 && hyperdht.request_in == 5 && hyperdht.response_time == 0.1",
+            test_env,
+        ) == ["6"]
+
+    def test_decoded_fields(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        capture = capture_file("hyperdht.pcapng")
+        checks = {
+            3: "hyperdht.delayed_ping.delay == 1250",
+            8: "hyperdht.closer_nodes.count == 2",
+            12: "hyperdht.peer_handshake.mode == 4",
+            14: "hyperdht.peer_holepunch.mode == 4 && hyperdht.peer_holepunch.id == 7",
+            16: "hyperdht.find_peer.peer.relay_count == 2",
+            18: "hyperdht.lookup_reply.peer_count == 2 && hyperdht.lookup_reply.bump == 42",
+            19: "hyperdht.announce.peer.relay_count == 2 && hyperdht.announce.bump == 42",
+            23: "hyperdht.mutable_put.seq == 5 && hyperdht.mutable_put.value",
+            25: "hyperdht.mutable_get.seq == 3",
+            26: "hyperdht.mutable_get.seq == 5 && hyperdht.mutable_get.value && hyperdht.mutable_get.signature",
+            27: "hyperdht.immutable_put.value",
+            30: "hyperdht.immutable_get.value",
+            31: 'hyperdht.plugin.name == "fixture-plugin" && hyperdht.plugin.version == 2 && hyperdht.plugin.command == 9 && hyperdht.plugin.value',
+            32: "hyperdht.plugin.response_value",
+            33: "hyperdht.unknown_command",
+            35: "hyperdht.trailing && hyperdht.trailing_bytes",
+        }
+
+        for frame, display_filter in checks.items():
+            frames = _frames(
+                cmd_tshark,
+                capture,
+                f"frame.number == {frame} && {display_filter}",
+                test_env,
+            )
+            assert frames == [str(frame)], f"field check failed for frame {frame}"
+
+        assert _frames(cmd_tshark, capture, "hyperdht && _ws.malformed", test_env) == []
